item.title: "Vile person of the year": Candace Owens targeted by Donald Trump with doctored TIME cover, calls her “low IQ”
item.description: Donald Trump reignited his feud with Candace Owens by sharing a doctored magazine cover and calling her “low IQ.” The attack followed criticism of her remarks about Brigitte Macron. Owens responded sharply online, escalating tensions as their public dispute continues to draw attention across political and media circles.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Ronaldo has three final career dreams he must fulfil before retirement, Messi already has the first
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is entering the final phase of his career with three clear goals still driving him forward: a first World Cup title in 2026, the pursuit of 1,000 career goals, and the rare chance of playing alongside his son at Al Nassr. Even at 41, he remains central for club and country, shaping both legacy and milestones.

item.title: Streamer iGumdrop takes her cooking from Twitch to MasterChef and impresses Gordon Ramsay
item.description: Twitch sensation iGumdrop, known for her online food streams, is now a contestant on MasterChef Global Gauntlet, representing Team Asia-Pacific. She impressed Gordon Ramsay with her wagyu beef satay, aiming to put Malaysian cuisine on the global map. Securing her white apron, iGumdrop proved her culinary skills extend beyond the internet.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: The real wall with ears: Ancient Roman walls can hear you from metres away
item.description: Ancient Roman structures, utilizing smooth stone and carefully shaped interiors, exhibit remarkable acoustic properties. Curved walls and vast domes guide sound, creating whispering gallery effects where even quiet voices travel with surprising clarity. This architectural design allowed performers in Roman theaters to be heard by large audiences without amplification.

item.title: Prosecutors claim 40TB of data linked to D4vd includes child pornography in shocking court update
item.description: Prosecutors unveiled a staggering 40 terabytes of evidence against D4vd, including disturbing claims of illegal child-related material found on his devices. The rapper faces serious charges, including murder and abuse of a minor, though he maintains his innocence. His defense team vows to contest the prosecution's narrative, which alleges a relationship with a girl under 14.

item.title: Hunter becomes the hunted: Five elephants crush 75-year-old millionaire trophy hunter to death during hunt
item.description: A 75-year-old American millionaire and trophy hunter, Ernie Dosio, died in Gabon after a sudden encounter with a herd of five elephants. While tracking a rare antelope, Dosio and his guide were charged by the elephants, resulting in Dosio being fatally trampled and his guide seriously injured. This incident highlights the potential danger of close encounters with these powerful animals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Peace talks back on? Trump sending envoys to Pakistan to meet Iran FM; Vance on standby
item.description: Senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Pakistan for crucial talks with Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi to revive negotiations amid escalating regional tensions. The diplomatic initiative aims to address Tehran's nuclear program and ease global market volatility. Despite overtures, the situation remains volatile with ongoing conflicts impacting vital shipping lanes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Italian Job: Could Pep Guardiola be next Italy boss after World Cup disaster? Big reset being discussed
item.description: Pep Guardiola has emerged as a surprise target for Italy as the federation considers a major reset after a third straight World Cup failure. With leadership changes underway, officials are reportedly exploring an ambitious move despite financial and contractual hurdles at Manchester City. The idea reflects a desire to redefine the national team’s direction ahead of a crucial appointment cycle.

item.title: Biobank Data Sale Scare: UK health trove briefly listed in China; watchdogs fear public trust hit
item.description: Sensitive UK Biobank health data, potentially affecting nearly 500,000 participants, was briefly listed for sale on a Chinese marketplace. British authorities acted swiftly to remove the listings, but the incident has raised fresh concerns about the security of the vast research database.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US court blocks Trump order suspending asylum access, cites right to apply
item.description: A US appeals court has halted President Trump's order barring asylum access at the southern border. Judges ruled immigration laws permit border asylum applications, and the President cannot unilaterally suspend this right. This decision offers a lifeline to individuals fleeing danger, ensuring they receive a hearing for their claims.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump Backs Royal Visit Reset: Ex-president bets on palace charm; Starmer rifts still loom
item.description: Donald Trump believes King Charles III's upcoming US visit will mend frayed Washington-London ties, despite trade, security, and policy disagreements. He praised the King as a "fantastic man" and "brave." While the royal tour aims to strengthen historic bonds, underlying tensions persist over immigration, energy, and foreign policy, with the US also eyeing tariffs on digital services.

item.title: Could Ronaldo play alongside his son at Al-Nassr next season? Reports say club planning step-up after 16th birthday
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo could soon share the pitch with his son as Al-Nassr consider integrating Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. into senior training from next season after he turns 16.
